subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Rubber: From Trees to Tires
description: A short lesson to help you apply Rubber: From Trees to Tires.

hook.text: Natural rubber comes from trees. Charles Goodyear cooked it with sulfur and invented vulcanization.

buildup.text: Raw rubber melts in heat and cracks in cold. Vulcanization cross-links polymer chains, making it stable.

discovery.text: Goodyear accidentally dropped rubber mixed with sulfur on a hot stove in 1839. The result was flexible and tough.

twist.text: Goodyear died in poverty. The Goodyear Tire company was named after him 38 years later — by someone else.

climax.text: Synthetic rubber now dominates. 70% of rubber is petroleum-based. Natural rubber still can't be fully replaced.

punchline.text: A kitchen accident put the world on wheels.

quiz.question: What does vulcanization do to rubber?
options: It bleaches rubber white for use in medical products
It cross-links polymer chains making rubber stable in heat and cold
It compresses rubber into sheets thin enough for gloves
